items.title: Google February 2026 Discover Core Update is Now Complete
items.summary: Google's February 2026 Discover core update rolled out over 21 days from February 5 and completed on February 27, marking the first Discover-specific core update affecting U.S. English users with plans for global expansion. It prioritizes locally relevant content from U.S.-based sites, reduces clickbait and sensationalism, and emphasizes in-depth, original content from expert sources on a topic-by-topic basis. The update has caused significant volatility in Google Search organic results, potentially impacting non-U.S. sites targeting U.S. audiences.

items.title: Discover Core Update Data, Sitemap Tips & AI Risks – SEO Pulse
items.summary: Early data from the February Discover core update indicates a decrease in unique U.S. publishers from 172 to 158, but an increase in unique content categories, benefiting specialized and local sites while clickbait reduction is less clear. Google may ignore sitemaps lacking 'new and important' content despite technical validation. Microsoft research highlights risks of hidden prompt injections poisoning AI assistants like Copilot and ChatGPT for biased recommendations.

items.title: How to Revise Your Old Content for AI Search Optimization
items.summary: Revise old content for AI search (AEO) by reformatting into clear, structured answers using a hub-and-spoke model for topical depth, self-contained chunks for retrieval, and concise summaries with factual tones. Prioritize content demonstrating expertise or proprietary insights, and refine metadata like titles and headings as context anchors for AI systems. This approach helps AI models easily extract and synthesize information from legacy pages.

items.title: Writing for GEO Feels Like Early SEO All Over Again
items.summary: Writing for Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and AI search mirrors early SEO's machine-focused tactics like keyword stuffing, prioritizing extraction over ranking and reader experience. Content creators should use question-based headings, direct first-sentence answers, standalone excerpt-ready sections, specific claims, and anticipate follow-ups while avoiding over-optimization. Test structures with AI tools but retain unique voice and nuance.

items.title: How to Increase Google Discover Traffic with Technical Fixes
items.summary: Boost Discover traffic by optimizing publisher profiles with accurate Knowledge Graph data, linking social media via Organization schema sameAs and footer links. Implement large hero images (1200px+ wide), max-image-preview:large meta tags, and matching Open Graph images with defined dimensions. Enhance transparency with author bylines, bios, images, schema, plus robust About Us pages and editorial policies.

items.title: Content & Marketing Trends for 2026
items.summary: 2026 content marketing trends highlight AI-powered search shifts, including benchmarks for AI referral traffic, Google AI Overview visibility, and impacts from generative answers on SEO and traffic. Marketers must adapt strategies to secure citations and mentions in AI responses amid automation and changing search behaviors. Focus on new skills, metrics, and brand engagement in this evolving landscape.

items.title: AI Models Can Spit Out Entire Novels Word-for-Word — and That’s a Big Legal Problem
items.summary: Recent studies from Stanford and Yale show leading AI models from Google, xAI, and Anthropic can reproduce up to 76.8% of bestselling novels like Harry Potter when prompted. This challenges claims that models only learn patterns without storing copies, fueling lawsuits with courts ruling it copyright infringement. The issue extends concerns beyond publishing to data privacy in other sectors.

items.title: 1 year, 1 publisher, 9,000 books: AI-generated titles flood Korean shelves
items.summary: One Korean publisher, Luminary Books, released about 9,000 AI-generated nonfiction titles in 2025, sparking concerns over quality, ethics, and exploitation of the legal deposit system. Booksellers like Aladin now require AI disclosure, and some publishers add guidelines for human oversight. The trend highlights debates on transparency and trust in AI-assisted publishing.

items.title: Literary agents ban use of AI in book submissions
items.summary: Several UK literary agencies have updated guidelines to reject submissions using generative AI for cover letters, synopses, or manuscripts, citing a rise in such entries flattening authors' voices. Agencies like Greene & Heaton and Bright Agency emphasize original human work, amid broader industry worries over AI training on copyrighted material. This reflects challenges in detecting improving AI as it impacts securing publishing deals.

items.title: AI in publishing: The Geological Society’s position
items.summary: The Geological Society supports responsible AI use in research and publishing but requires disclosure in manuscripts and prohibits listing AI as authors or uploading content to LLMs. Reviewers must verify AI-assisted work and avoid confidentiality breaches, with the society reserving rights over its content for AI training. Human oversight remains essential to uphold integrity amid risks like hallucinations and copyright issues.

items.title: Indies Win! Harlequin to Close Historical Romance Line
items.summary: Harlequin plans to close its historical romance line in fall 2027 after nearly 40 years, as indie authors dominate via Kindle Unlimited with faster releases and lower ebook prices. Traditional publishing's slow timelines and higher costs hinder competition in shifting romance trends. Readers increasingly follow indie authors over imprints, marking challenges for mass market traditional lines.

items.title: WTF is pay per ‘demonstrated’ value in AI content licensing?
items.summary: Publishers and AI companies are testing 'pay per demonstrated value' licensing, compensating based on content's relevance to AI queries, citation frequency, and type rather than flat fees. Factors include timeliness, uniqueness, and query value, with platforms like TollBit measuring via vectors for dynamic pricing. This seeks fair revenue amid traffic losses from AI answers and training data debates.

items.title: BAFTA Controversy: Racial Slur Aired During Presentation
items.summary: During the BAFTAs, an attendee with Tourette syndrome shouted the N-word as actors Michael B. Jordan and Delroy Lindo presented, and the BBC aired the unedited footage. Wunmi Mosaku, a co-star in Sinners, slammed the BBC at the SAG Actor Awards for the decision, calling it 'incredibly painful' and 'exploitative' that affected Black viewers worldwide. The incident sparked widespread debate and criticism of the broadcaster's handling.

items.title: Star Trek: Starfleet Academy Faces Backlash and Drops from Charts
items.summary: Paramount+'s Star Trek: Starfleet Academy has fallen from the Top-10 streaming charts amid criticism of poor writing, acting, and inclusion of political lectures. Fans highlighted elements like cadets learning theater, adults reading children's books, and a male Klingon in a dress as examples of unwanted preachiness. The show is described as reaching new lows in the franchise.

items.title: Hollywood Woke Remakes Like Snow White and The 'Burbs Flop at Box Office
items.summary: Remakes such as Disney's Snow White, which lost $170 million, and the 2026 reboot of The 'Burbs are cited as examples of politically correct films prioritizing agendas over entertainment. These projects demonize conservatives and inject moral lectures, alienating audiences and leading to significant financial losses for studios. The article argues for merit-based storytelling to reverse the trend.

items.title: God of War TV Series First Look Sparks Fan Backlash
items.summary: The first-look image of Ryan Hurst as Kratos in Amazon's God of War series drew significant online backlash. Hurst responded on Instagram, advising fans not to believe everything seen on the internet. The reaction highlights fan sensitivities to adaptations of popular games.

items.title: Scream 7 Achieves Franchise-Best $97M+ Global Box Office Debut
items.summary: Scream 7 roared to a record-breaking $97 million-plus global debut, marking the best opening in the franchise's history. The success comes amid a competitive box office landscape. It underscores strong audience interest in the horror series.

items.title: SAG Actor Awards: Sinners Wins Top Film Prize Amid Upsets
items.summary: Sinners claimed the top film prize at the SAG Actor Awards, with The Studio and The Pitt leading in TV categories. Notable upsets included Michael B. Jordan beating Timothée Chalamet. Viola Davis was stunned on stage during the event.

items.title: How Your Small Business Can Use AI To Compete With Industry Giants
items.summary: Small businesses can use AI tools like ChatGPT to replicate functions of large organizations, such as marketing, customer service, and data analytics, at a fraction of the cost—around $500 monthly versus six-figure salaries. By mapping out missing functions, building AI systems for each, and focusing human efforts on core differentiators like product innovation, owners protect high-value time while AI handles commodity work. This approach leverages speed for faster shipping and adaptation, turning size into a disadvantage for giants.

items.title: How the rise of AI-native software could give SMBs enterprise-level power
items.summary: A Deloitte study predicts a surge in AI-native software applications, challenging traditional SaaS and benefiting SMBs with enterprise capabilities at lower costs via competition, low-code platforms, and specialized solutions. AI-native vendors introduce new interfaces, results-driven pricing, and AI orchestration, shifting from license-based models. SMBs gain from more options but must address data readiness, integration, governance, and AI literacy challenges.

items.title: Orca Advisor Launches to Deliver AI-Powered Business Intelligence for Small Businesses and Institutions
items.summary: Orca Advisor has launched its Orca Snapshot Report, an AI-powered business health assessment providing small and mid-sized businesses with insights into finance, strategy, risk, and operations. It benchmarks performance against industry data, identifies gaps and risks, and delivers prioritized recommendations for decision-making. The tool makes high-quality advisory accessible without large analyst teams.

items.title: Ignite Business Software Launches AI-Powered Operating System to Transform Mid-Market Service Firms
items.summary: Ignite Business Software launched an AI-powered enterprise operating system with vertical SaaS for mid-market service firms in construction, home services, and professional services. Using the C.L.E.A.R.™ framework, it streamlines processes like lead vetting, scheduling, and data management for firms without IT departments. It improves efficiency and revenue tracking for businesses generating $600K to $10M+ annually.

items.title: Forwardly Launches AI Agent to Help Replace Manual Work with Automation and Move Businesses Forward
items.summary: Forwardly launched an AI Agent that automates finance tasks by auto-coding transactions, processing complex invoices, and learning from feedback on over 1 million transactions. It detects anomalies, trends, and risks in real-time, handles approvals, and provides dashboards for visibility. This reduces manual effort for business finance teams, enhancing productivity and control.
